title: Elephants Engineer Their Ecosystems Even in Death - Nautilus
gist: A PNAS study from UC Santa Barbara sampled soil and plants at 40 elephant carcass sites in Kruger National Park over nearly eight years to show that dead elephants keep shaping savanna ecosystems.

insights.claim: Elephants are ecosystem engineers that trample trees, loosen soil with their tusks and create trails and watering holes.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Elephant loss has ecosystem-level consequences relevant to conservation finance.

insights.claim: A new PNAS study finds elephant carcasses continue to sculpt savannas long after death, based on nearly eight years of soil and plant sampling at 40 carcass sites in Kruger National Park.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: The excerpt does not give the specific findings, so treat the effect size as unknown.
insights.locator: According to a new study published in the Proceedings
